newsitem.title: USA: MCA Records enters licensing pact with Hendrix family.
newsitem.headline: MCA Records enters licensing pact with Hendrix family.

text.p: MCA Records Tuesday entered a licensing pact for the catalog of the late guitar icon Jimi Hendrix, who galvanized listeners worldwide in the 1960s with his revolutionary music.

The global agreement also establishes a joint venture record label between MCA Records and the Hendrix family-run company, Experience Hendrix, to sign and develop acts under a new Experience Hendrix imprint.

"Jimi Hendrix is one of the seminal figures of rock history. Today, his music is as fresh and innovative as ever as he continues to influence and inspire generation after generation of musicians," said Zach Horowitz, president of Universal Music Group.
Universal Music Group is a unit of The Seagram Co. Ltd. and encompasses MCA Records, GRP Recording Co., Geffen Records, Universal Records, Interscope Records among others.

Under this agreement, the classic Jimi Hendrix catalog will be re-released on MCA Records worldwide in conjunction with Experience Hendrix, which recently assumed control of the famed guitarist's recordings 27 years after his death.
"Jimi Hendrix's music is an essential part of every guitarist's musical vocabulary," said Jay Boberg, President of MCA Records.

"Every single kid that picks up a guitar will find Hendrix at some point. And because of this timelessness, Jimi's records sell millions each year and actually sell more now than when he was alive. Our goal at MCA Records is to grow that audience year after year and to widen his already enormous influence and appeal," he said.
Outside of the United States, the catalog will be released and marketed through Universal Music International.
This pact marks the first time Hendrix's recordings will be released under the authority of his family and gives the family long-sought creative control.
Planned for release in 1997 are new products sanctioned by Experience Hendrix, including never-released music and music re-mastered and re-packaged.
This agreement also marks the first time the catalog will be released on compact discs made from the first generation original masters.
The first new global release under the agreement will be "First Rays of The New Rising Sun," the last album recorded by Jimi Hendrix before his death.

Despite his phenomenal critical and commercial success, Seattle-born Hendrix was continually frustrated with himself and ambivalent toward his popularity. His death in 1970 in London was related to a drug overdose.
